title: groundstation field test №13: 20 new asks on 0.28.0, 5 of them mining
heading: THE FIELD TEST №13
sub: groundstation · 20 prompts · 20 live artifacts · 7 swipes, 2 timelapses, 2 3D views, 5 maps, 2 postcards, 2 briefs · October 26, 2026 · Development Seed labs
lede: Twenty new questions the way real people ask them, five of them about mining: an open pit year by year, lithium ponds, a tailings flow, a reclamation check and a Superfund pit lake. Run live and in-process on main at 0.28.0, the night after field test 12. New since 12: 0.27.0 fixed the small things 12 found (compare_dates takes stack_facts, write_archive takes max_cloud_cover and dates the archive in UTC, a Zarr time outside the store's range is refused with the range named), and 0.28.0 has the geocoder say what kind of place each candidate is, so a feature word like lake or glacier picks the feature. The real findings: render_postcard on Planetary Computer ignores the band, colours and crop you ask for and does not say so; HRRR answers a six-day-old date with today's numbers and only a caveat says it snapped; the word lake in Lake Charles now picks the lake over the city; the brief page and conditions_brief search different radii, so one says CALM and the other all_clear false; the point rule throws away a small real extent; and compare_dates picked different tiles on two identical calls. 7 swipes, 2 timelapses, 2 3D views, 5 maps, 2 postcards and 2 briefs; 16 of the 20 carry the Stack panel (the briefs on their linked maps). Every returned block is verbatim tool output and every card keeps its stumble. A field test is a showcase, not CI: it shows what the tools do today.

cases.answer: The valley box is greener now than before the dam failed: mean NDVI is 0.6328 on 2025-07-01 against 0.5591 on 2018-08-15, a rise of 0.0737 (13.2%, both from the tool). Measured from the first dry season after the flow, 2019-09-09, it was 0.4851, so the rise since then is 0.1477 (30.4%, tool). By my arithmetic (not tool output) the post-flow drop was 0.5591 - 0.4851 = 0.0740, and the gain since is about twice that. That is NOT the share of the mud footprint that has greened: the number is one mean over a 6.5 km box that also holds forest, pit and roads, and I did not outline the flow, so I cannot give a percentage of the covered ground.
cases.learning: The ask's baseline answers a different question. A 2018 "before" is pre-failure, so the delta says the box is now above its old level, not how much of the flow area has recovered; I reran with 2019 as the post-flow start, and the swipe artifact is that second run. Neither run says what share of the mud footprint is green, because compare_dates returns one clipped mean for the box and has no polygon mask, so the user's "how much of the ground" needs a footprint outline the tool does not take.
cases.shows: compare_dates (clipped means, hand bbox, two baselines) · swipe artifact · Stack panel

cases.prompt: Hobet mine in Boone County was supposed to be reclaimed. Is vegetation actually coming back on the old mountaintop removal area since 2016?
cases.answer: Probably yes, but the evidence is thin: NDVI over a hand-drawn box on the bare benches rose from 0.7432 (2017-07-26) to 0.8371 (2025-08-10), a gain of 0.0939 (12.6%, from the tool). I could not start at 2016 because the Sentinel-2 L2A catalog returned nothing for 2016 over this area, so the earlier date is 2017. I also could not locate Hobet by name; the box is my own pick from a true-colour preview, not a permit boundary, and I have no permit acreage to set against it. The 2017 scene is partly cloudy in the preview I looked at, which may pull its mean down.
cases.learning: There is no place yet for a caller's own notes beside a map. I passed three free-text facts in stack_facts and none of them show in the Stack panel. That is by design: stack_facts are honest provenance flags (geocoded, events, weather, passes, terrain, snapshot) that tell the panel which components to credit, not a notes field, so an inspector's "box hand-picked, no 2016 scene" has nowhere to go but the subtitle or the answer. Two smaller stumbles: the geocoder found nothing for Hobet in three phrasings, and there is no 2016 scene to compare against, so "since 2016" became 2017.
cases.shows: compare_dates stack_facts (provenance flags, not notes) · clipped means · geocode refusal and hand bbox · Stack panel

cases.answer: In the box around Wahweap and the main channel, about 5.0% of the pixels read as water on 2026-05-11 against 3.6% on 2022-05-02, so there is more water surface now, roughly 1.4 times as much by pixel share. The tool's own 38.0% is the same ratio; I got 1.38 times from 0.0501 / 0.0363 (my arithmetic, not tool output). The box is about 22 km by 24 km, roughly 540 km2, so 0.0138 of it is about 7.5 km2 of extra water (my arithmetic from the box size, not tool output). The tool warns that a baseline this small makes the percentage swing on noise, so quote the 0.0138, not the 38%. The index threshold of zero is my choice, and steep canyon shadow can also read as water, so treat this as a good estimate, not a surveyed area.

cases.answer: In the 2011 and 2026 Landsat true-colour scenes the lake looks smaller and the pale exposed lakebed looks broader in 2026.
